needs.heading: What you'll need
items: Control of your domain, so you can publish one small public file, poppy.json, on it over HTTPS.
For level 2, a check in front of your APIs that verifies the signed header assistants send with every request. It needs no sign-in server.
For level 3, a sign-in server that speaks OAuth, the standard behind most "Sign in with..." screens, and sign-in and consent pages on your own site, where customers approve what an assistant may do.
Developer time that grows with each level: about a day for level 1, then days to weeks for each level after it.

page.checksIntro: These are the checker's rows for this level, by their ids in the check catalog. Building what this level describes, and following the guides it links, is what makes them pass. A row that checks something you do not offer does not apply. The checks not run yet were written for Draft 0.2 and link its pages; they will be rewritten for Draft 0.3 before the checker runs them.

groups.optIn: Checked only when the site owner opts in
groups.signedIn: Signed-in checks, not run by the checker yet

hosted.before: Rather not run a sign-in server yourself?
hosted.linkText: Ora can host Poppy on your domain, with your login, in front of your existing APIs.
hosted.label: Hosted option

levels.title: Be findable
levels.summary: Publish one public file that tells assistants where to go, and, if you run a sign-in server, have it confirm that the file is yours.
levels.size: Small. A few JSON documents, served over HTTPS. A day or less if you already run an OAuth server, and less without one.

levels.title: Let agents in, signed out
levels.summary: Assistants sign every request with a Session header that says who they are and which person and session the request is for. You check it before you rely on it, with no sign-in server needed.
levels.size: Medium. A check in front of every API that verifies signed headers against each assistant's published keys. Days to weeks, less if one gateway does it for all your APIs.

levels.title: Let people sign in
levels.summary: People sign in with plain OAuth on your own pages, choose what each assistant may do with their account, and can disconnect it later.
levels.size: Large. Sign-in and consent pages, scope descriptions, refresh tokens, sign out, and an account settings page. Weeks, less if your OAuth server already does most of it.

levels.title: Optional surfaces
levels.summary: Let an assistant's browser join its session, let assistants talk with your own agent, and ask for the person's approval before you act.
levels.size: Varies. Each surface is its own project: days for the browser join, weeks for conversations or operations.
